body: Don't we use an RGBA16 buffer for FSR1? This looks like it will apply debanding before doing FSR1 upscaling

In the case of:

- Forward+
- HDR 2D: disabled
- SMAA: disabled
- FSR1: enabled

Tonemap destination buffer will be RGBA16 (with nonlinear sRGB encoding) and FSR1 destination buffer will be RGBA8.

So to answer your question in short: yes, RGBA16 for FSR1. And yes, debanding before FSR1 upscaling.

FSR1 and MetalFX (Spatial) have not been modified to apply debanding, so it needs to be applied earlier than optimal. That is, debanding needs to be applied by tonemap, even though it would be better for debanding to be applied after FSR1 or MetalFX.

I decided it was simplest to not modify FSR1 to include a debanding step, like I did for SMAA, because FSR1 follows the same code paths as MetalFX and MetalFX cannot be modified to support debanding without another pass and intermediate buffer.

There is another potential issue that SMAA, FSR1, and MetalFX may be provided either linear or nonlinear sRGB-encoded values (based on `use_hdr`), even though they may be designed to work with only one or the other. But that's outside the scope of the debanding work that I was doing...

The comment makes it sound like debanding is being performed whether we are using Forward+ or Mobile. From what I understand, it isn't supposed to happen on Forward+. I would say either specify it doesn't happen on Forward+ or remove the `if` statement, because I don't think `DEBANDING_MODE_10_BIT` does anything on Forward+ anyways.
